Though notice is served, none appears for respondent No.2 - original complainant.
2. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the matter is taken up for final disposal forthwith.

3. By way of this application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as "Cr.P.C."), the applicants have prayed to quash and set aside the complaint being FIR No. I- 04 of 2017 registered with DCB Crime Police Station, Ahmedabad City, for the offences under Sections 406, 420 and 114 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and all the consequential proceedings arising therefrom.

4. At the instance of respondent No.2, FIR came to be filed against the applicants, wherein, it is alleged that, brother of the complainant i.e. Natvarbhai Ambalal Patel went to Surat for business Maheshbhai Ramnivas Beriya vs State Of Gujarat on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26016115/

It is further alleged that, payment of the purchased goods is being paid within 15-20 days and accordingly, making demand from the applicants, they had not paid the same and ultimately, the applicants had in all paid Rs.4,20,000/- as against the total due amount of Rs.17,67,273/- and therefore, outstanding amount of Rs.13,47,273/- which is unpaid by the applicants and hence, FIR came to be filed against the applicants.
5.
Heard Mr. Sunil Agrawal, learned counsel for the applicants and Mr. H.K.patel, learned APP for the respondent State.

6. Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted that, the applicants have been falsely enroped in the offence with a view to pressurize them to release the payments though they are not required to be made to the original complainant.

There was business transaction between the parties took place in the year 2015, whereas, the complaint has been filed in the year 2017 and therefore, after a delay of 2 years, complaint has been filed which is an afterthought.
He further submitted that, applicant No.2 is not connected in any way with the complainant and has not done any business transaction with the complainant.

The applicants have done business transactions with the opponent No.2 for last 2-3 years and during that period, the applicants have made full and final payments of the goods purchased from complainant and at the relevant point of time, there was no any such grievance raised by the complainant.

Applicant No.1 is the father of applicant No.2 and applicant No.1 had business relation with the complainant and however, with a view to harass applicant No.1, name of applicant No.2 has been falsely roped in the offence.
Further, the dispute is of civil in nature and instead of exhausting civil remedy, the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/3552/2022 ORDER DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined complainant has filed criminal proceeding.

He also submitted that,
even act of breach of trust may not be resulted into a penal ofence of criminal breach of trust unless there is evidence of manipulating act of fraudulent.
In view of the above contentions, Mr. Agarwal prays to allow present application and quash the FIR against the applicant, as prayed for, in this application.

7. Learned APP appearing for the respondent-State has opposed present application and contended that, the applicants by hatching criminal conspiracy, committed an offence of criminal breach of trust and fraud.

Thus, prima facie involvement of the applicants is established and therefore,
present application may not be entertained.

8. Having heard learned counsel for both the sides and going through the allegations levelled against the applicant, it prima facie appears that there is no nexus or relationship between the applicant No.2 and complainant and no evidence is produced on record, which connects the applicants in the alleged offence.

There was business transaction between the parties which took place in the year 2015, whereas, the complaint has been filed in the year 2017 and therefore, after a delay of 2 years,
complaint has been filed, which is an afterthought.
Further, applicant No.2 is not connected in any way with the complainant and has not done any business transaction with the complainant.

Applicant No.1 is the father of applicant No.2 and applicant No.1 had NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/3552/2022 ORDER DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined business relation with the complainant and however, with a view to harass applicant No.1, prima facie it appears that, name of applicant No.2 has been falsely roped in the offence.
Further, the dispute is of civil in nature and instead of exhausting civil remedy, the complainant has filed criminal proceeding.
He also submitted that, without there being specific evidence of manipulating act of fraudulent, the act of breach of trust may not be resulted into a penal offence of criminal breach of trust.
Further, the dispute is of commercial in nature and only with a view to recover the money of goods, complaint came to be initiated.
It is needless to say that liability recommends difference between the simple payment of investment of money and entrustment of the property.
In absence of any fraudulent entrustment or dishonest intention as well as in absence of contractual relationship for the obligation between the accused and complainant, no offence is made out.

9. In view of the above, this Court is of considered view that without any nexus or relationship between the applicant No.2 and complainant, he has been arraigned as accused only with an intention to recover the money.

Therefore, if the proceedings are allowed to continue against the applicants, the same will be nothing short of abuse of process of law and travesty of justice and therefore, this is a fit case to exercise inherent power under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C for quashing of criminal proceedings.

10. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case as well as the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of (i) Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab & Anr., reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303, (ii) Rekha Jain Vs. State of Karnataka, reported in 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 468, (iii) Rekha Jain Vs. State of Karnataka, reported in 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 468, (iv) State of Haryana & Ors. Vs.
Bhajanlal & Ors., [1992 Suppl. 1 SCC NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/3552/2022 ORDER DATED:
12/06/2024 undefined 2020], and (v) Lalit Chaturvedi & Others vs. State of Uttar Pradesh &
Another, in the opinion of this Court, further continuation of criminal proceedings, more particularly offence under Sections 406 and 420 of IPC against the applicant/s in relation to the impugned FIR would cause unnecessary harassment to the applicant/s.
